title: MFA required for all users
rationale: Passwords alone are phished or reused daily. Requiring a second factor for every user on every cloud app stops the large majority of account takeovers.
remediation: Create a Conditional Access policy: Users = All users (exclude two break-glass accounts), Target resources = All cloud apps, Grant = Require multifactor authentication. Start in report-only, review sign-in logs for a week, then switch it on.

title: MFA required for Global Administrators
rationale: Admin accounts are the keys to the whole tenant. They must never be usable with a password alone.
remediation: Create a Conditional Access policy targeting directory roles (at least Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, Security Administrator, Exchange/SharePoint/Intune Administrator) on all cloud apps with Grant = Require multifactor authentication.

title: Legacy authentication blocked
rationale: Legacy protocols (IMAP, POP, SMTP AUTH, older Office clients) cannot do MFA, so attackers use them to bypass it with password spraying.
remediation: Create a Conditional Access policy: Users = All users, Conditions > Client apps = Exchange ActiveSync clients + Other clients, Grant = Block access. Check the sign-in logs (filter Client app) first for service accounts that still rely on legacy auth.

title: Phishing-resistant MFA for admins
rationale: Push and SMS MFA can be phished with adversary-in-the-middle kits. FIDO2 keys, Windows Hello for Business and certificates cannot.
remediation: Register FIDO2 keys or Windows Hello for Business for all admins, then create a Conditional Access policy for admin roles with Grant = Require authentication strength > Phishing-resistant MFA.

title: Sign-in risk policy enforced
rationale: Entra ID Protection flags sign-ins from anonymous IPs, impossible travel and token replay. Acting on that signal stops attacks in progress.
remediation: With Entra ID P2: create a Conditional Access policy for all users with Conditions > Sign-in risk = Medium and High, Grant = Require MFA (or authentication strength) and Session = Sign-in frequency every time.

title: User risk policy enforced
rationale: A user flagged as high risk (for example leaked credentials) should be forced to prove identity and reset the password.
remediation: With Entra ID P2: create a Conditional Access policy for all users with Conditions > User risk = High, Grant = Require MFA + Require password change.

title: Between two and four Global Administrators
rationale: One admin is a single point of failure; many admins multiply the attack surface. Day-to-day admin work belongs in least-privilege roles.
remediation: Keep two to four Global Administrators including a cloud-only break-glass account. Move other admins to scoped roles (Intune Administrator, Exchange Administrator, User Administrator) and use PIM for just-in-time elevation where licensed.

title: SMS sign-in method disabled
rationale: SMS codes are vulnerable to SIM-swapping and interception. Authenticator app or passkeys are stronger alternatives.
remediation: Entra admin center > Protection > Authentication methods > Policies > SMS: disable, after confirming users have registered Microsoft Authenticator or a passkey.

title: Users cannot register applications
rationale: App registrations can be granted access to tenant data. Creating them should be an admin decision, not something every user can do.
remediation: Entra admin center > Identity > Users > User settings: set 'Users can register applications' to No. Grant the Application Developer role to those who need it.

title: User consent to apps restricted
rationale: Consent phishing tricks users into granting a malicious app access to mail and files. Restricting consent closes that path.
remediation: Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > Consent and permissions: set user consent to 'Do not allow' or 'Allow for verified publishers, for selected permissions', and enable the admin consent workflow.

title: Guest invitations restricted
rationale: If anyone can invite guests, external access grows without oversight.

params.passText: Only admins and Guest Inviters can invite guests.

remediation: Entra admin center > External Identities > External collaboration settings: set guest invite restrictions to 'Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users'.

title: Guest directory access restricted
rationale: Guests should not be able to enumerate your users, groups and structure.
remediation: Entra admin center > External Identities > External collaboration settings: set guest user access to 'Guest users have limited access' or 'Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects'.

title: Users cannot create new tenants
rationale: Shadow tenants created by users fall outside your governance and can be abused.

params.failText: Any user can create a new Entra tenant.

remediation: Entra admin center > Identity > Users > User settings: set 'Restrict non-admin users from creating tenants' to Yes.

title: Compliant device required for access
rationale: Tying access to a managed, compliant device means a stolen password alone is not enough to reach company data.
remediation: After compliance policies are in place, create a Conditional Access policy: Users = All users, Target = Office 365 (or All cloud apps), Grant = Require device to be marked as compliant (optionally OR hybrid joined). Pilot in report-only first.

title: Disk encryption (BitLocker) enforced
rationale: A lost or stolen laptop without encryption is a data breach. BitLocker makes the disk unreadable without the key.
remediation: Intune > Endpoint security > Disk encryption: create a BitLocker policy (silent encryption, XTS-AES 256, recovery key escrow to Entra ID) and assign it to all Windows devices.

title: Antivirus policy (Defender) enforced
rationale: Centrally enforced real-time protection, cloud-delivered protection and tamper protection prevent users or malware from switching Defender off.
remediation: Intune > Endpoint security > Antivirus: create a Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy (real-time protection, cloud protection high, PUA block, tamper protection on) and assign it to all Windows devices.

title: Firewall policy enforced
rationale: A managed firewall on every network profile limits lateral movement once a single device is compromised.
remediation: Intune > Endpoint security > Firewall: create a Windows Firewall policy that enables the firewall on Domain, Private and Public profiles with inbound blocked by default, and assign it to all Windows devices.

title: Local admin passwords managed (LAPS)
rationale: A shared local admin password across devices lets one compromised laptop unlock them all. LAPS gives every device a unique, rotated password.
remediation: Enable LAPS in Entra ID device settings, then Intune > Endpoint security > Account protection: create a Local admin password solution (Windows LAPS) policy with backup to Entra ID and assign it to all Windows devices.

title: Attack surface reduction rules enforced
rationale: ASR rules block the techniques most malware relies on: Office spawning processes, credential theft from LSASS, obfuscated scripts.
remediation: Intune > Endpoint security > Attack surface reduction: create an ASR rules policy. Start the rules in Audit mode, review Defender reports for two weeks, then switch them to Block.

title: Devices onboarded to EDR
rationale: Endpoint detection and response gives you visibility and the ability to isolate a device during an incident.
remediation: Connect Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to Intune, then Intune > Endpoint security > Endpoint detection and response: create an onboarding policy (auto from connector) and assign it to all Windows devices.

title: Windows Update ring assigned
rationale: Unpatched devices are the most common way in. Update rings make patching automatic with controlled deferrals and deadlines.
remediation: Intune > Devices > Windows updates > Update rings: create rings (pilot / broad) with quality update deferral 0–7 days and a deadline of at most 7 days, and assign them to all Windows devices.

title: Windows compliance policy assigned
rationale: Compliance policies define what a healthy device is (encryption, OS version, Defender). Without one, Conditional Access has nothing to enforce.
remediation: Intune > Devices > Compliance: create a Windows 10/11 compliance policy (BitLocker, Secure Boot, minimum OS version, Defender antimalware, firewall) and assign it to all Windows devices or users.

title: Devices without a compliance policy are non-compliant
rationale: By default, a device with no assigned compliance policy counts as compliant — a silent gap in Conditional Access.

params.passText: Devices without a compliance policy are marked non-compliant.
params.failText: Devices without a compliance policy are treated as compliant.

remediation: Intune > Devices > Compliance > Compliance policy settings: set 'Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as' to Not compliant.

title: Mobile compliance policies assigned
rationale: Phones and tablets reach the same mail and files as laptops and need the same minimum bar (PIN, encryption, no jailbreak).
remediation: Intune > Devices > Compliance: create iOS/iPadOS and Android Enterprise compliance policies (passcode, encryption, jailbreak/root detection, minimum OS) and assign them.

title: Non-compliant devices below 10%
rationale: Policies only help if devices actually meet them. A high non-compliance rate means controls exist on paper only.
remediation: Open Intune > Devices > Monitor > Noncompliant devices, group by failing setting and fix the top causes (often BitLocker, OS version or stale devices). Retire devices that have not checked in for 90+ days.
